component.name: FujiNet Go MSX
component.summary: Self-contained MSX / MSX2 / MSX2+ with built-in FujiNet

description.p: An MSX, MSX2 or MSX2+ with FujiNet built in: mount disk images from TNFS servers or the local SD folder, configure everything through the embedded FujiNet web UI, and boot straight into FujiNet's CONFIG screen. C-BIOS is bundled, so every machine boots with no manufacturer firmware required.

Emulation is provided by openMSX, with FujiNet attached over its own cartridge device on loopback TCP. The debugger understands all three video chips this family of machines shipped with -- the MSX1 TMS9918A and the MSX2/MSX2+ V9938/V9958 -- including their register sets, command engine, and palette RAM.

screenshot.caption: FujiNet CONFIG running on the emulated MSX2
The built-in Z80 + V9938/V9958 VDP debugger

description.p: Debugger: a FujiNet tab shows every FujiBus packet between the MSX and FujiNet, both ways, with hex.

Cartridge ROMs mounted from FujiNet CONFIG boot again. Booting any .rom crashed the app, because the FujiNet cartridge device read a mapper type the firmware no longer sent. MSX megaROMs named with their mapper, such as game[ASCII8].rom, now switch banks correctly, and an untagged ROM loads as a plain cartridge.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves back onto upstream master. The previous build came from force-mbedtls-3, a branch that was never merged, so the runtime had been standing still while upstream moved on. The Mbed TLS 3.x requirement it was branched for has landed, and the device-chain rework and the Drivewire cassette media format arrive with it.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves to a firmware build that refuses to compile against Mbed TLS 4.x. That release removed the low-level crypto headers the runtime's TLS backend needs and split the rest into a separate library, so a machine whose system Mbed TLS had moved to 4.x could produce a build with broken TLS instead of a clear failure. The build now finds a 3.x install, or stops and says so.

This is a large jump in the bundled runtime, which had been pinned well behind the others. Programs running on the emulated MSX gain the Gmail and Google Drive network protocols and the CALENDAR, GCAL and ICAL calendar protocols, alongside the accumulated fixes of the intervening firmware work.

Fixes FujiNet going silent for any program launched from the FujiNet CONFIG ROM. The emulated cartridge stopped decoding its own receive and status registers once a user ROM was mapped in, so a program could send a request but never see the answer and would wait for it forever. Also picks up a console command to toggle the config ROM and two config ROM refreshes.

Fixes the macOS build refusing to launch on real hardware ("You can't use this version of the application ... with this version of macOS"): the app bundle's minimum macOS version was left unset and defaulting to whatever SDK the CI runner's Xcode shipped, which could be newer than a tester's actual OS. The minimum is now pinned to macOS 11.

First release of the MSX desktop app: a headless openMSX core driving MSX/MSX2/MSX2+ with C-BIOS bundled, FujiNet built in and joined over its own cartridge device, and a debugger covering the Z80 CPU and the full TMS9918A/V9938/V9958 VDP family.
